department: Department of Earth Science and Engineering

deadline.value: Applications are accepted all year, but funding has deadlines. The President's PhD Scholarship rounds close 2 Nov 2026, 11 Jan 2027 and 1 Mar 2027. The department's Janet Watson Scholarships (Home or Overseas fees) need your application, with a supervisor's agreement, by 11 Jan 2027.
deadline.quote: Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 2 November 2026 and are awarded a scholarship will be notified by 31 January 2027. | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 11 January 2027 | Applicants who apply by 23:59 (UK time) 1 March 2027

also.quote: If the supervisor agrees, submit your PhD application via the Imperial application portal by 11 January 2027.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for this field; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Start by contacting a faculty member about a research topic, and submit the online application only after they have shown enough interest in you.
supervisor.quote: Regardless of the source of funding, interested students should begin the application process by contacting a faculty member to discuss the potential research topic. | Online applications should only be submitted after the potential academic supervisor has expressed sufficient interest in your application.

funding.value: Funding comes from research grants (open to overseas students only in exceptional cases), college and department scholarships, and CDTs. The department's Janet Watson Scholarships cover Home or Overseas fees plus a 3.5-year UKRI-rate bursary, are merit-based and usually go to MSc holders.
funding.quote: PhD positions funded through research grants may be available to overseas students in exceptional cases. | Not all potential PhD projects listed on the website have funding associated with them

also.quote: Bursary for 3.5 years (UKRI rate) plus tuition fees for 3 years (Home or Overseas).
Awards are based on exceptional academic merit and/or potential. Applicants will usually have completed an MSc or equivalent.

entry_route.value: You need at least a 2:1 (or equivalent) undergraduate degree in a field suited to your research; it does not have to be in Earth sciences. Department scholarship winners usually also hold an MSc.
entry_route.quote: Applicants should hold an undergraduate degree in a field appropriate to the intended area of PhD research, with a classification of at least upper-second-class, or the equivalent.

notes: The department admits about 40 PhD students a year. Research covers planetary, environmental, solid-earth and climate science, subsurface geoscience and engineering, energy, mineral extraction and computational science. Contact: ese-pgr-admin@imperial.ac.uk.
